title: About us - Kwanlin Dün First Nation
edition: Nation website, About us page, fetched 13 September 2026

extraction.command:
python3 -c 'import re,html,sys
p=sys.argv[1]
t=open(p,encoding="utf-8",errors="replace").read()
t=re.sub(r"(?is)\x3c(script|style|noscript)[^\x3e]*\x3e.*?\x3c/\1\x3e"," ",t)
t=re.sub(r"(?i)\x3cbr\s*/?\x3e","\n",t)
t=re.sub(r"(?i)\x3c/(p|div|li|h[1-6]|tr|section|article)\x3e","\n",t)
t=re.sub(r"(?s)\x3c[^\x3e]+\x3e"," ",t)
t=html.unescape(t)
t="\n".join(re.sub(r"[ \t\xa0]+"," ",l).strip() for l in t.split("\n"))
t=re.sub(r"\n{3,}","\n\n",t).strip()+"\n"
sys.stdout.write(t)' content/sources/kdfn-about-us.html

knownStaleness.topic: The statement draws on three passages of one page, and only one of them is the recorded quote
knownStaleness.problem: content/levels/the-north.json quotes `We acknowledge the Tagish Kwan as the original people who live and occupy the lands that define our Traditional Territory, alongside the headwaters of Chu Ni'ikwan (today, the Yukon River). Our people have been here for millennia.` Its clause about the City of Whitehorse comes from a second passage on the SAME page - `KDFN's Traditional Territory encompasses the Yukon's capital and economic heartland, the City of Whitehorse` - and the meaning of `Kwanlin` comes from a third - `Our ancestors called the area Kwanlin, which means "running water through canyon" in Southern Tutchone`. A FactSource carries one quote, so two of the three are here rather than in the level document. THIS IS STILL BETTER THAN EVERY LEVEL BEFORE IT: content/levels/vancouver.json's statement rests on two DOCUMENTS from two different bodies and only one can be registered (OQ-VANCOUVER-4). Here all three passages are one page published by the one nation the statement names.
knownStaleness.action: verify all three passages against this cache, not only the recorded quote.

knownStaleness.topic: The Ta'an Kwach'an Council is not named, and the silence is deliberate
knownStaleness.problem: The Ta'an Kwach'an Council is a self-governing Yukon First Nation with its headquarters in Whitehorse and a traditional territory of about 12,079 sq km reaching west to the confluence of the Takhini, and roughly half its citizens live in Whitehorse. THIS PAGE DOES NOT SAY THAT WHITEHORSE IS INSIDE THAT TERRITORY - it names the Ta'an Kwach'an only in the history of Chief Jim Boss - and the Council's own history page at https://taan.ca/history/ does not say it either: it names Taa'an Man (Lake Laberge) as the heart of the territory and gives its bounds by four place names rather than by the city. A level carries ONE nationSource, and naming a second nation's territory on a page that does not state it would be the invention this register exists to prevent. So the level names one nation and is silent about the other. That is the same shape as content/levels/alberta-foothills.json's silence about the Metis Nation of Alberta, and it is recorded here for the same reason.
knownStaleness.action: do not resolve the silence in either direction from this cache. If a page published by the Ta'an Kwach'an Council states that its traditional territory takes in Whitehorse, the statement is widened and this flag is closed; until then no copy on this level says or implies that one nation's territory is the only one here.

knownStaleness.problem: The page carries governance, land-claim and service content beside the passages quoted, so extractedTextSha256 will move for reasons that have nothing to do with them. The claims themselves - that the nation's traditional territory encompasses Whitehorse, that its people have been here for millennia, and what Kwanlin means - are standing statements and do not expire, which is why the level's fact is NOT marked volatile.
knownStaleness.action: when the hash stops matching, re-read the three passages named in the first flag before assuming a claim moved.

liveChecks.consequence: THE WEAKEST OF THE SIX CHECKS AND IT SAYS SO HERE RATHER THAN IN A REPORT NOBODY KEEPS. retrievedAt is 2026-09-13 and this check is 2026-09-13: the cache was taken the same day, so re-fetching established only that the URL served the same 157,548 bytes twice in one day, hashing both times to 455bc9eb1762549ca55dbddc0cc0e61fc781ad196e9a8ee7a168b20b9f02b786. That is not an interval and it is not evidence about maintenance. What it IS good for is the third flag, which predicts the digest will move for reasons unrelated to the three passages: the clock on this entry starts today and the next check is the one with something to say. The page's own article:modified_time is 2026-04-08, five months before the cache, which is the only real evidence here and is the page's claim about itself rather than a fact. ONE DISCREPANCY FOUND, NOT FIXED: the first staleness flag transcribes the quoted river name as “Chu Ni’ikwan”, with an apostrophe and two plain vowels; both the live page and the cached extraction read “Chu Níikwän”, with an acute i and an a-diaeresis and no apostrophe at all. The shipped quote is unaffected - verify-content reports every source.quote contiguous in its extraction, so content/levels/the-north.json carries the page's spelling - and it is the REGISTER's instruction prose that mis-transcribes the name a verifier is told to check against. It is a nation's own word for its own river and the verifier does not edit quotations, so it is reported and left. Same flag, same sentence: the extraction renders "Kwanlin , which means" with a space before the comma, an artefact of the tag stripper crossing an emphasis tag, and the flag's prose silently closes it up. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: all three flags leave upstream absent, treated as "revises", so "About us" stays on ADR-0016 section 2 row 1 - correctly, since the third flag says in as many words that this is a live nation website - and content/levels/the-north.json's territory claim is still on an unarmed row-1 clock.
